nodedef_library_validation: Full validation of node instances against the MaterialX standard nodedef library (verifying that a node's declared inputs/outputs match a registered nodedef, type-checking connections against declared input/output types) is out of scope for this pass. This pass fixed the write-path data-loss bug for nodedef elements themselves (FACT-MTLX-101: a nodedef now survives load->write->reload with its name, category, declared type, and interface inputs/outputs intact) but does not implement semantic validation against the ~800-node standard library defined by the spec. No real-file consumer need for library validation has surfaced yet; revisit if a use case requires rejecting a document with an undeclared/mismatched node instance.
look_collection_variant_semantic_resolut: look/collection/variant elements now survive a load->write->reload cycle with full structural fidelity (FACT-MTLX-101's generic element preservation covers <look>, <collection>, <variantset> and their children verbatim -- nothing is silently dropped). What remains out of scope is *semantic* resolution: evaluating which geometries a <materialassign> actually targets, resolving <collection> membership predicates, or substituting <variant> values into a graph. This is a materially larger feature (requires a geometry/selector evaluation engine this codec does not have) and was not part of the four confirmed defects this sprint targeted.
xinclude_multi_file_resolution: MaterialX documents may reference other .mtlx files via <xi:include href="..."/> to compose a library from multiple files. This codec parses a single file/bytes/string source only and does not resolve xi:include references into a merged document. Out of scope for this pass -- the four confirmed defects (write-path data loss, graph connection resolution, node category/data-type confusion, volumematerial/legacy shaderref support) are all single-document concerns. Revisit when a multi-file real-world corpus (e.g. a full DCC material library with a shared nodedef library file) becomes a driving use case.
nodegraph_level_interface_input_modeling: MaterialX nodegraph-level <input> elements (declaring a graph interface parameter that inner nodes reference via interfacename) are currently parsed generically into the node graph's 'nodes' bucket rather than a dedicated 'interfaces' list, since distinguishing them was not one of the four confirmed defects. get_connected_node()/resolve_connections() (FACT-MTLX-102) correctly resolve interfacename references in the common case where the interface name matches an entry in that bucket, but a nodegraph-level interface input is not modeled as a semantically distinct construct from a node. Revisit if a consumer needs to enumerate a node graph's public interface parameters separately from its internal nodes.
